method: Authorized static reverse engineering only; no firmware/device execution. Existing prose was used as hypothesis, instruction exports as evidence.

scope.owned: librrnavdrv and AppProxy map callers; no librobopersist/librrslamdrv annotations
type_ownership: /shared/MapFlowBackupRowView (observed20-byte ABI view, not original C++ class)

findings.summary: LoadSLAMMap performs grid/interface load before flag/config changes and persistence load; failures do not roll back prior stages.
details: Core mutex at +0x2c8 and secondary manager mutex (from 0x170850) are acquired when thread-support global is nonzero; lock errors throw. It marks event/state 0x83, suspends selected workers, and calls SLAM virtual slot +0x10 before the grid wrapper.

0x68544 calls 0x1a621c. Zero wrapper result bypasses catalog/persistence and enters common cleanup. Wrapper 0x1a621c calls virtual +0x68, returns bool(result_code==0); unsigned result<=3 only selects log text.
Signed flag >1 at 0x6854e..0x68556 sets catalog current immediately. Flag==1 instead reconciles stored manager flag and current catalog flag. Negative/zero flags do not use either update branch.

0x68562 queries per-map state; 0x6856e or 0x687a0 adjusts core map-state/recovery bytes. 0x685a0 sets all map-using status to 0, 0x685aa sets selected map using status to 1, then filename wrapper 0x1a71b4 and PersistLoadMapInfo at 0x685ba.

Persistence false logs and returns zero through common cleanup, with no grid/catalog/config rollback in this function. Persistence true restores pose/downstream state; flag1 clears core recovery marker at 0x6891a; success value is one. Poses include signed halfword conversion, not unsigned coordinates.
Common cleanup resumes workers, restores the earlier manager condition, clears event 0x83 and unlocks. None of these caller observations proves disk durability or a transaction.

findings.summary: The flag-1 catalog choice is an in-process initialized stored-flag predicate, not a direct disk/catalog-validity condition.
details: Constructor clears byte manager+0x22 and sets stored word +0x28 to -1. Getter at 0x1a5fd4 is unsigned LDRB; getter 0x1a6018 loads +0x28.
0x1a5fdc writes +0x22=1 and +0x28=native_flag, then logs only. It is called following successful grid save for a destination >1; saving last-map destination1 records the catalog current flag.

Flag1 load: if +0x22 nonzero, SetSharedCurrentMapFlag(stored+0x28). If zero, GetSharedCurrentMapFlag is copied into manager via 0x1a5fdc. This can leave catalog current flag2 while files for flag1 were selected.
The initializer predicate does not alone show whether the associated catalog or grid files are valid or mutually consistent.

findings.summary: Native multi-save attempts grid/state stages sequentially, then persistence API acceptance; partial changes survive some failures.
details: 0x67144 rejects native flag1 when manager+0x1f or core+0x271 is set. If allowed, virtual grid save +0x6c is called through 0x1a60c4; only result_code==0 is success.
After successful grid save it stores the manager flag, snapshots shared robot/dock poses, and invokes per-map metadata/config helper 0x1a7488 under observed core+0x2e0 synchronization.

0x6732c locks core+0x2c8, calls 0x67144 for each destination, skips later stages after first false, and only if all succeed calls PersistSaveMapInfo(vector) at 0x673de. Earlier successful grid writes are not deleted on a subsequent grid-stage failure.

If PersistSaveMapInfo returns false, it iterates all flags and calls SLAM virtual +0x70 (delete); delete returns are ignored. Single-save 0x67484 does grid/state first then one-flag persistence and same delete-on-persistence-false behavior.
Calls into persistence/grid are ownership boundaries. This lane verifies API call order, not detached-writer finish, write success, fsync, or a cross-file commit.

findings.summary: Startup last-map seed 0x20bac0 is interior; existing instructions support candidate entry 0x20babc, but no baseline function exists.
details: 0x20babc loads a PIC constant, 0x20babe sets r2=0, 0x20bac0 pushes registers, 0x20baca sets r1=1, then 0x20bad6 calls LoadSLAMMap(core,1,0). The first two instructions are needed by the body, so push alone is not the true-entry proof.
Constructor 0x20f57c installs Thumb pointer0x20babd at 0x20f960 for state3 (LoadLastMap). Reference and instruction dumps are in discovery-nav4, discovery-startup-final, discovery-boundary-nav.

Load false clears state+0x320/+0x321/+0x322 and sets +0x323 before subsequent state selection. Success also queries map1 metadata at 0x20bb48. Later state selection considers bytes +0x32a,+0x331,+0x320,+0x321,+0x322,+0x323,+0x31c.

String OnStateLoadLastMap at0x2bc8dc is referenced at0x20bbd8; common return at0x20bb40 and stack-check-fail call0x20bce6 bound the collected body. No function creation or startup C reconstruction was performed.
Preceding state selector starts at candidate0x20b780 (constructor Thumb pointer0x20b781); bytes0x20b778 are literal-pool words mistakenly decoded as instructions. Do not use0x20b778 as an entry.

findings.summary: Core+0x271 prevents overwriting last-map while recovery is needed; the external configuration key mapping is unresolved.
details: 0x663b8 sets byte+0x271 and0x6640c clears it with DMB barriers. Diagnostics name them SetNeededToRecoverLastMap and ResetNeededToRecoverLastMap.
Core initializer0x705e8 clears+0x271 at0x70756. Successful flag1 LoadSLAMMap clears it after persistence restore, and clear-map-state0x66464 also clears it.
In state callback0x20c3d8: if relocation unsuccessful and state+0x321 or+0x322 is set, marks state+0x324 and calls0x663b8 at0x20c500. Original floating-point/register/stack ABI is not reconstructed.

Already collected strings/map-strings.txt places need_recover_map and RoboController.runtime.need_recover_map in RoboController variants, not owned/pinned navigation/AppProxy. No binary-key-to-core-field proof is asserted; no expansion to those binaries.

findings.summary: Ordinary load queues load then save-last, but reports ok without waiting for the final save result.
details: Command registration0x637ba..0x637d4 maps load_multi_map to Thumb0x4fbf9. Handler validates access/state/params and external flag via catalog-owned0x3b908, computes native=external+2, creates series keyed by request words, appends callbacks0x3cc74 and0x39b84 and invokes0x24450.
First callback gates activity via0x3cc18, sends0x01033107, sends load0x02033204(native flag) through0x39aa4; returns1. One callback remains, so runner waits.
Accepted load result handled by0x56a84 requires length16 and result==1. It advances series; false results fail the pending series, not execute the save-last callback.

Save-last callback0x39b84 updates timestamp under proxy+0xf54, ClearCleanRouting, SetSharedCurrentMapFlag(native), sends save0x02033203(flag1) at0x39c1c and updates application map state0x8c46c; returns1.

Critical runner instructions0x24488..0x24498 compare deque begin/end AFTER popping callback: equal forces r0=0, otherwise r0&=1. The save-last step was last: its requested wait is overridden, causing immediate success callback even though no save result was received.

Configured success callback0x4705c calls response formatter0x46e9c with literal ok (0xf3398) and clears action lock. Formatter calls0x3f70c to hand response to sender. Transport/network internals are intentionally not followed.

This is a complete AppProxy-local command/queued-result/reply path, conditional on the externally supplied load result. The transport bridge to navigation and returned-result provenance remain unresolved, so it is not a request-to-hardware proof.

findings.summary: Recovery has no-op, ordinary-load fallback, and distinct-backup three-step branches with different completion meanings.
details: Command recover_multi_map registered at0x6383a..0x63852 -> Thumb0x51629. Handler validates requested external flag, adds2, then calls catalog-owned0x3c568 with native request and an output slot. It compares selected_native-2 to requested_external.

If selected==requested and shared current==requested+2, immediately sends ok at0x519b8, no load/save/database operation. If selected==requested but current differs, uses the ordinary two-step load/save-last series and its early save acknowledgment.

If backup differs, validates request as primary and selection as backup through0x3b908, then queues0x68c14(load selected backup),0x3c7a0(save destination flags[1,requested_native]),0x3a5c0(DB). The selected backup is recomputed in the first callback; concurrent catalog changes are not ruled out.
0x68c14 calls destination helper0x68b48 before sending load. That helper forwards a flag vector to unresolved0x68ae8; do not claim cancellation completion or flush.

On successful load result,0x3c7a0 updates timestamp, routing and catalog current, then sends save-set0x02033212 via0x3c6bc with destinations[1,requested_native]. One DB callback remains, so runner honors returned1 and waits.

After accepted save-set result (0x55500 length16,result1), DB callback0x3a5c0 invokes0x3a430 and returns0 unconditionally. Then series success sends ok. This result covers reaching DB helper return, not a checked DB-write success or asynchronous persistence-file completion.

findings.summary: Reached backup DB operations assign ID=native_flag-2; errors are logged but terminal recovery still advances.
details: 0x3a430 calls map-buffer preparation helper0x8cddc( map_object,1 ), then sets local external_id=native_flag-2. Blob pointer is map_object+0x30002c and size word map_object+0x48002c; scratch read capacity0x80000.

0x23070 selects existing bakmaps row. On read failure, insert0x22f84; on read success with blob_size0, also insert; nonzero blob_size uses update0x23210. Return codes control only logging in0x3a430; the wrapper is void and0x3a5c0 returns0 regardless.

Existing global SQL pointers verified in discovery-boundary-app/data.txt:0x12082c -> select id,map from bakmaps where id=?;0x120830 -> insert into bakmaps(id,map) values(?,?);0x120838 -> update bakmaps set map=? where id=?. Statement pointers database+0x138,+0x134,+0x140 respectively.
Insert/read/update lock database+0x160; insert/update expect step101, read expects100, then reset statements. Update binds signed ID via ASR r3,r2,#31.

Important failure discrepancy: update normal unlock uses the acquired+0x160 pointer, but error epilogue at0x2329e forms database+0x178 before pthread_mutex_unlock at0x232a2. This is an observed offset mismatch, not proof what the two mutex objects represent or a firmware repair.
No schema/history behavior beyond the reached bakmaps queries was explored. No SQLite transaction, WAL policy, sync mode or durability conclusion is claimed.

findings.summary: The DB helper writes a current application-facing map buffer, not a native grid or persistence region record.
details: Inference from bakmaps SQL, native-minus-two ID, application-map object buffer offsets and0x8cddc preparation call, consistent with existing ASSESSMENT analysis. This lane did not decompile the buffer-generation internals or verify its encoding. Do not use a DB blob as evidence native files were updated.

findings.summary: Result handling advances/fails a keyed pending series; local locks are not a cross-process storage transaction.
details: Result handlers compare payload length+8==16 and result+0x18==1. Request key low/high are+0xc/+0x10 and native flag is+0x14. Failure calls0x245f8 with text and deletes pending series; success calls0x24450. Legacy fallback processing only runs if keyed series was not handled.

0x69c88 is treated as single-map result handling based on legacy branches and series use; its diagnostics confusingly say load map result failed. Operation identity must not come from that copied string alone.

0x24450 removes completed series under mutex+0x4c; callback/step execution itself is outside this particular erase lock.0x24350 scans timeout paths under same mutex and calls configured timeout hook. These locks protect local bookkeeping, not all writers or files.

Error callback pointer Thumb0x4afa9 is installed in constructor0x63f90. Existing instructions at0x4afa8..0x4b01d send error through0x4ad88 and clear action lock; no baseline function exists, no generated error-callback C claimed.

findings.summary: Exportable immediate startup paths are annotated, while missing startup state entries stay explicit.
details: 0x83940 gates catalog-current loading on manager/lab/use-new-map branches and signed current>=2, calls0x68428 at0x83b8a; load failure enters reset state. It later initializes shared robot/dock poses, so do not equate it to the isolated last-map loader.
0x8339c calls LoadSLAMMap(core,-2,1), then SaveMap(core,1), then sets catalog current from saved manager word+0x30; load/save results are ignored.

0x6905c calls LoadSLAMMap(core,captured_flag,1) at0x69076 and stores result in completion capture+0x2c. Data0x304b78 points to Thumb0x683e1, which has neither defined baseline instructions nor a function. Raw bytes/proposal only; the final completion sender is not proven.

findings.summary: Nontrivial AppProxy IPC-to-navigation task/result bridge is not closed in pinned owned programs.
details: AppProxy load request0x02033204, save0x02033203, save-set0x02033212 are emitted with original request keys. Their dispatch through RoboController to navigation events, result-message ID registration and delivery back to AppProxy are not established end to end.

Only agreed missing entries are delegated centrally. No new function creation or ABI guesses were made to cover this bridge. Confirmed AppProxy result-dependent paths and confirmed navigation call order are separate pieces of evidence, not an invented atomic chain.

corrections_to_prior_prose: ASSESSMENT seed0x20bac0 is interior. Candidate true entry0x20babc is supported by leading PIC/r2 initialization plus state registration; missing baseline function remains a gap.
ASSESSMENT unresolved flag1 selector is narrowed to manager+0x22 initialized flag, with manager+0x28 stored word; not an arbitrary catalog validity or disk-existence check.

SUPERVISION application load/recovery completion unknown is partially closed locally: ordinary load replies after load result and final save send, not final save result; distinct-backup recovery waits load/save-set results then invokes unchecked DB helper.
No-op recover success can report ok without performing any load/save/DB operation.
Earlier provisional lane comments described0x68b48 as cancellation/IPC. Final comments explicitly leave0x68ae8 helper semantics unresolved; no such cancellation proof exists in collected exports.
Earlier provisional lane comment mislocated the update error-unlock operand at0x232e2; actual instruction is0x2329e, followed by unlock0x232a2.
Do not interpret0x20b778 literal-pool bytes as a function entry; collected constructor points to0x20b781 (candidate even0x20b780).

Decompiler void defaults for grid/load/save/series helpers were corrected at ABI level only after inspecting preserved result registers and return paths. Unknown C++ layouts and ambiguous callback/startup ABIs remain unreconstructed.
unresolved_edges: How the emitted AppProxy IPC is mapped by RoboController to navigation tasks/results, including exact result registration and correlation, remains unresolved.
Candidate missing startup0x20babc, completion callback0x683e0 and error callback0x4afa8 require central metadata recovery; no generated C for them is supplied.
need_recover_map configuration-key mapping is outside pinned owned inputs; relation to NavCore+0x271 is not proven.

Underlying grid virtual targets, persistence background completion, cross-process semaphore/buffer behavior, catalog setter disk semantics and disk durability require other lanes/integration; this lane does not equate API success with completed writes.
Destination helper0x68b48 ->0x68ae8 behavior remains unresolved. Backup selection is performed twice; no catalog-wide lock across the entire series was established.
0x69c88 single-map result identity is inferred from use/legacy branches despite misleading log strings; exact wire registration is unresolved.
Database failure-path mutex+0x178 versus acquired+0x160 discrepancy is confirmed at instruction level; resulting runtime behavior was not tested.
Other command strings save_map/get_multi_maps_list/get_multi_map/save_as_multi_map were bounded for registration/context only, not traced as complete alternative paths.

limits: Static checks do not prove robot runtime behavior.
No cross-file transaction or completed durable disk write is claimed.
No data captured from private rooms, credentials or unrelated device state was included.
Reconstructed names are inferred analysis names under30 characters; imported/surviving symbols were not replaced.
